Silver price and the gold/silver ratio

Silver tends to underperform gold during risk-off periods and outperform during rallies — a pattern sometimes called "gold on steroids." The gold/silver ratio is a useful context check: when it's historically elevated (above 70–80), silver has often had more upside than gold in subsequent moves.

Track the ratio live: Gold/Silver Ratio →

Why silver is more volatile than gold

Silver's market is much smaller than gold's. The same volume of buying or selling produces larger percentage moves. Silver also has significant industrial demand — solar panels, EVs, electronics — that adds economic-cycle sensitivity gold doesn't have to the same degree. For a full explanation: Why Silver Is More Volatile Than Gold.
